name: Longer Laser B1 20W
tagline: 20W Longer's large-format diode: bigger bed than Ray5 for sign-sized projects
tldr: Longer Laser B1 20W is the 20W SKU on the Longer longer laser b1 line. Longer's large-format B1 20W diode: this profile is the 20W SKU only; Longer also sells 30W and 40W B1 machines separately. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: Everyday engraving plus reliable light cutting on wood, leather, and dark acrylic

priceRange.note: 20W optical module: verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Cheapest way into the 450 × 440 mm B1 frame: $479.99 basic set (Longer store, October 2026)
Fine 0.08 × 0.1 mm spot, per Longer's spec sheet
Extension kit and touch screen available as add-ons
cons: Slow fills in our tests: ~14–32 mm/s, so a 10 × 10 cm photo takes ~18–28 min
Our cut benchmark is far below Longer's 15 mm one-pass claim
Touch screen and extension kit cost extra on the basic set
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 20W SKU on Longer Laser B1. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Use air assist for cuts, lower scan speed for photo engraving. Multiple passes at moderate speed beat one aggressive pass. Check the flagship tier’s cut benchmark if you quote production times to customers.

editorialDepth.advantages: Longer Laser B1 20W is the versatile hobby / side-business SKU: clean engraving and light wood or leather cuts with comparable benchmarks on Maker Atlas.
editorialDepth.limitations: Open-frame: glasses and exhaust required. Upgrade path to 30W or 40W if cutting takes over. Not a CO₂ replacement for clear acrylic or heavy thick-stock production.

faq.question: How thick does the B1 20W really cut?
faq.answer: Longer's spec sheet claims 15 mm basswood in one pass and 35 mm acrylic maximum. In our benchmarks a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes about 9–15 min at 2–3 mm/s, so treat 8 mm basswood and 5 mm dark acrylic as practical limits in passes; 15 mm needs ideal settings and air assist.

faq.question: Which B1 20W set should I buy?
faq.answer: On Longer's store in October 2026: Basic set $479.99, Pro set $649.99, Pro Max set $869.99, and Basic set plus IR module $799.99 for jewellery and metal marking. An extension kit ($109.99) and a touch screen ($39.99) are sold separately.

faq.question: B1 20W or B1 30W?
faq.answer: Both share the 0.08 × 0.1 mm spot and the 450 × 440 mm area. The 30W basic set cost $90 more ($569.99), is rated for 20 mm basswood in one pass instead of 15 mm, and fills at ~39–88 mm/s in our tests against ~14–32 mm/s. If you engrave most of the time, the 20W is enough.

standoutFeatures.title: Large bed at entry price
standoutFeatures.body: 450 × 440 mm working area from $479.99, extendable with Longer's $109.99 extension kit.

standoutFeatures.title: Detail-friendly spot
standoutFeatures.body: 0.08 × 0.1 mm according to Longer, the finer of the two spot sizes in the B1 range.

standoutFeatures.title: IR module bundle
standoutFeatures.body: Longer sells a Basic set with IR module ($799.99) for engraving jewellery and metal.
